_meta.purpose: How SparkFraud authenticates against each origin. The 'header set per origin/realmid' is currently scattered across app.js:buildHeaders, background.js:driveOrderResolution cleanup, background.js:fetchJson gscope branch, and every dispatcher recon script. This file is the single source of truth.
data_safety_rules: NEVER log or persist cookie VALUES — only names.
NEVER include x-authheader/x-authtoken values in telemetry, fixtures, docs, or commit messages.
Captured headers in chrome.storage.session are session-scoped and die with Edge — that is intentional.

swift_dispatcher._purpose: Calling swift.walmart.com Spark Dispatcher endpoints. Header-based auth — NO cookies attach (confirmed in notes/api_endpoints.md:179-180).
swift_dispatcher.cookie_lookup_note: Cookie names from gscope are inconsistent in case. app.js:215 lowercases all keys before lookup. NEW consumers MUST do the same.
swift_dispatcher.source: notes/api_endpoints.md:144-180, captured from natural SPA requests.

gscope_oms_drive._purpose: Calling gscope provider-oms/orders by driving the Order Resolution UI in a helper tab and harvesting the natural response. SLOW PATH.
gscope_oms_drive.cookies_attached_via: Same-origin: the helper tab IS a gscope tab, so the browser attaches all cookies (incl. HttpOnly JSESSIONID) automatically.
gscope_oms_drive.headers_required: None set by us — the SPA's interceptors set the right x-realmid and other headers when its own fetch fires.
gscope_oms_drive.tab_lifecycle: Open fresh background tab → drive form → capture response from window.__SPARK_CAP → close tab. NEVER reuse a tab (notes/api_endpoints.md 'Reusing the Order Resolution tab' — second drive hangs).

gscope_replay._purpose: Replaying gscope endpoints with captured headers via in-gscope-tab fetch. FAST PATH (subsequent calls after drive-the-UI has captured headers once).
gscope_replay.cookies_attached_via: Same-origin: fetch runs inside an open gscope tab via chrome.scripting.executeScript, so cookies attach automatically.
gscope_replay.headers_required: Captured at slow-path drive time; persisted in chrome.storage.session.omsHeaders (session-scoped).
gscope_replay.strip_list_rationale: Chrome won't allow setting these — browser-managed or pseudo-headers from HTTP/2. Sending them throws or is silently ignored.
gscope_replay.stale_header_recovery: On 401/403 with cached headers, clear chrome.storage.session.omsHeaders and fall through to slow path (background.js:306).

gscope_in_tab_generic._purpose: Generic gscope endpoint via in-tab fetch with minimal headers (just content-type). Used by fetchJson when no captured headers exist.
gscope_in_tab_generic.headers_NOT_set_and_why: Dispatcher-specific x-* headers (x-realmid: DISPATCHER_WEB_UI etc.) would be wrong for OMS / other gscope endpoints. The server rejects requests with mismatched realmid (notes/api_endpoints.md:240-244).
gscope_in_tab_generic.open_question: Which gscope endpoints accept cookie-only auth and which require their realmid-specific headers? Currently unknown — most non-OMS gscope endpoints not yet driven.

walmart_consumer._purpose: Calling walmart.com consumer product pages for og:image scrape.

cookie_extraction_strategy._purpose: Workaround for Walmart-managed Edge's gutted chrome.cookies API. Documented here so future consumers don't re-discover.
cookie_extraction_strategy.problem: chrome.cookies.getAll({}) from extension SW returns only 2 cookies for the entire profile (Edge corp policy).
cookie_extraction_strategy.workaround: Read non-HttpOnly cookies via chrome.scripting.executeScript injected into a gscope tab (document.cookie returns them all in-page). Merge with chrome.cookies.getAll for HttpOnly cookies.
cookie_extraction_strategy.preconditions: At least one tab open on https://gscope.walmartlabs.com/* and that tab is responsive (we race against a 5s timeout per tab and try each one).
